question: Which part of the Constitution of India deals with rights of citizenship of certain persons who have migrated to India from Pakistan?
solution:
The correct answer is __**PART II**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** rights of citizenship of people who migrated to India from Pakistan are covered in Part II **of the Constitution of India, in Article 6
 
• **Part II of the Constitution of India covers citizenship and includes Articles 5–11**.
 
• **Article 6 deals with the citizenship of people** who migrated to India from Pakistan after the partition.
 
• **Article 6: **
 
 
• The person, their parent, or grandparent must have been born in India as **defined in the Government of India Act of 1935**
 
• If the **person migrated before July 19, 1948**, they must have been an ordinary resident of India since their migration
 
• If the person migrated on or after July 19, 1948, they must have registered as a citizen of India before the Constitution came into effect
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The parts of the Indian Constitution are:** 
 
• **Part I:** The Union and its Territory, which includes articles 1–4
 
• **Part II: **Citizenship, which includes articles 5–11
 
• **Part III: **Fundamental Rights, which includes articles 12–35
 
• **Part IV: **Directive Principles of State Policy, which includes articles 36–51
 
• The **Constitution of India has 25 parts, 12 schedules, and 448 articles as of November 2022**.
 
• The **Constitution was originally formed with 22 parts, but was amended and expanded over time**.
